Minister of State Petroleum Resources (Gas), Rt. Hon. Ekperikpe Ekpo, gave the assurance when he received the Board and Management of Axxela Group, led by Chairman Nzan Ogbe, in Abuja during the week.
Ekpo welcomed Axxela’s transition to indigenous ownership, saying Nigerian control could strengthen the company’s ability to mobilise local resources and investment in support of President Bola Tinubu’s economic development agenda.
He also assured the company of the Ministry’s support in addressing operational challenges and creating an enabling environment for genuine investors in the gas sector.
Ogbe commended the Minister’s leadership and reaffirmed Axxela’s commitment to deploying natural gas for industrial growth, transportation, domestic cooking and other critical sectors of the economy.
However, he sought the Ministry’s intervention in resolving conflicting interests across the gas value chain, which he said continued to pose challenges to the company’s operations.
The appeal highlights a broader policy concern: although Nigeria has positioned natural gas as a transition fuel and industrial growth driver, operators still face regulatory, commercial and coordination frictions across processing, transportation, distribution and last-mile supply.
Axxela operates across the gas value chain, including processing, transmission and distribution, and serves industrial and commercial customers through its pipeline infrastructure. Its acquisition by BlueCore Gas InfraCo was supported by a $285 million debt-and-equity financing package, underscoring the scale of capital required to expand Nigeria’s gas infrastructure.
